packs.title: AWS interview
packs.blurb: Common AWS interview questions (IAM, VPC, S3, compute, data).

questions.text: How does IAM policy evaluation work?
questions.rubric: Explicit deny always wins. Then allow from identity or resource policies. SCPs limit the max permissions in an account. Permission boundaries cap a principal. Missing allow is deny.
questions.answer: Explicit deny always wins. Then allow from identity or resource policies. SCPs limit the max permissions in an account. Permission boundaries cap a principal. Missing allow is deny.

questions.rubric: Temporary credentials for a role, optionally with MFA and an external ID. Cross-account access and CI (GitHub OIDC) assume roles instead of storing AKIA keys.
questions.answer: Temporary credentials for a role, optionally with MFA and an external ID. Cross-account access and CI (GitHub OIDC) assume roles instead of storing AKIA keys.

questions.text: What is a Service Control Policy?
questions.rubric: An Organizations guardrail on what an account can ever do, even for root. It does not grant; it intersects. Use it to forbid leaving the org or disabling CloudTrail.
questions.answer: An Organizations guardrail on what an account can ever do, even for root. It does not grant; it intersects. Use it to forbid leaving the org or disabling CloudTrail.

questions.text: When do you use S3 Standard versus Intelligent-Tiering versus Glacier?
questions.rubric: Standard for hot. Intelligent-Tiering when access is unknown — it moves objects automatically. Glacier for archive with retrieval delay. Lifecycle rules automate the slide.
questions.answer: Standard for hot. Intelligent-Tiering when access is unknown — it moves objects automatically. Glacier for archive with retrieval delay. Lifecycle rules automate the slide.

questions.rubric: Yes for new PUTs and overwrites/deletes since 2020 — read-after-write. It is not a database: no cross-key transactions. Design for object immutability (new key per version).
questions.answer: Yes for new PUTs and overwrites/deletes since 2020 — read-after-write. It is not a database: no cross-key transactions. Design for object immutability (new key per version).

questions.text: How do you encrypt S3 objects?
questions.rubric: SSE-S3 (AWS-managed), SSE-KMS (your CMK, audit), SSE-C (customer key each request), or client-side. Bucket default encryption plus denials of unencrypted PUTs. KMS costs and rate limits matter.
questions.answer: SSE-S3 (AWS-managed), SSE-KMS (your CMK, audit), SSE-C (customer key each request), or client-side. Bucket default encryption plus denials of unencrypted PUTs. KMS costs and rate limits matter.

questions.rubric: A time-limited signed URL that grants that action (GET/PUT) without making the object public. Expiry and HTTPS only. Do not log the query string.
questions.answer: A time-limited signed URL that grants that action (GET/PUT) without making the object public. Expiry and HTTPS only. Do not log the query string.

questions.text: What is S3 Block Public Access?
hints: On by default in new accounts.
questions.rubric: Account/bucket settings that ignore public ACLs and policies. Turn it on unless you run a static website with a conscious public policy.
questions.answer: Account/bucket settings that ignore public ACLs and policies. Turn it on unless you run a static website with a conscious public policy.

questions.text: How do SQS and SNS differ?
questions.rubric: SQS is a pull queue (competing consumers, buffer). SNS is push pub/sub (fan-out). SNS → SQS when one event must reach several independent workers with their own retries.
questions.answer: SQS is a pull queue (competing consumers, buffer). SNS is push pub/sub (fan-out). SNS → SQS when one event must reach several independent workers with their own retries.

questions.text: When do you use EventBridge instead of SNS?
questions.rubric: When you need content-based routing, SaaS partners, scheduled rules, or archive/replay. SNS is simpler topic fan-out. Many designs: producer → EventBridge → SQS.
questions.answer: When you need content-based routing, SaaS partners, scheduled rules, or archive/replay. SNS is simpler topic fan-out. Many designs: producer → EventBridge → SQS.

questions.text: What is an SQS dead-letter queue?
questions.rubric: After maxReceiveCount failures the message goes to a DLQ for inspection. Without it, poison messages loop forever. Alarm on DLQ depth.
questions.answer: After maxReceiveCount failures the message goes to a DLQ for inspection. Without it, poison messages loop forever. Alarm on DLQ depth.

questions.text: When do you need SQS FIFO?
questions.rubric: When order and exactly-once (dedup) matter inside a message group. Lower throughput than standard. Standard is at-least-once and best-effort order — make consumers idempotent.
questions.answer: When order and exactly-once (dedup) matter inside a message group. Lower throughput than standard. Standard is at-least-once and best-effort order — make consumers idempotent.

questions.text: When is Lambda a better fit than ECS?
questions.rubric: Short, spiky, event-driven work with idle-scale-to-zero. ECS/Fargate for long-running, custom runtimes, or predictable always-on. Lambda has timeout, payload, and cold-start limits.
questions.answer: Short, spiky, event-driven work with idle-scale-to-zero. ECS/Fargate for long-running, custom runtimes, or predictable always-on. Lambda has timeout, payload, and cold-start limits.

questions.text: How do you mitigate Lambda cold starts?
questions.rubric: Provisioned concurrency, smaller packages, keep the runtime warm, avoid VPC unless needed (or use Hyperplane ENIs). Measure; don't guess. SnapStart for Java.
questions.answer: Provisioned concurrency, smaller packages, keep the runtime warm, avoid VPC unless needed (or use Hyperplane ENIs). Measure; don't guess. SnapStart for Java.

questions.text: API Gateway HTTP vs REST vs ALB?
questions.rubric: HTTP API is cheaper/simpler JWT. REST API has usage plans, API keys, richer auth. ALB can target Lambda too and is good when you already live in VPC/ECS. Pick by features, not habit.
questions.answer: HTTP API is cheaper/simpler JWT. REST API has usage plans, API keys, richer auth. ALB can target Lambda too and is good when you already live in VPC/ECS. Pick by features, not habit.

questions.rubric: ALB is L7 (HTTP, path, host, WAF). NLB is L4 (TCP/UDP, static IPs, extreme throughput). GWLW for inline appliances. Don't put NLB in front of HTTP routing needs.
questions.answer: ALB is L7 (HTTP, path, host, WAF). NLB is L4 (TCP/UDP, static IPs, extreme throughput). GWLW for inline appliances. Don't put NLB in front of HTTP routing needs.

questions.text: What does an Auto Scaling group actually scale?
questions.rubric: EC2 (or mixed) capacity from a launch template, using CPU, custom metrics, or SQS depth. Health checks replace bad instances. It is not ECS or Lambda scaling — those have their own.
questions.answer: EC2 (or mixed) capacity from a launch template, using CPU, custom metrics, or SQS depth. Health checks replace bad instances. It is not ECS or Lambda scaling — those have their own.

questions.text: What is an Availability Zone versus a Region?
questions.rubric: A Region is a geography with multiple AZs — isolated data centers with independent power/network. Multi-AZ is the default HA story. Multi-region is DR and latency.
questions.answer: A Region is a geography with multiple AZs — isolated data centers with independent power/network. Multi-AZ is the default HA story. Multi-region is DR and latency.

questions.rubric: Your isolated network: CIDR, subnets, route tables, gateways. Public subnets have a route to an IGW; private do not. Security groups and NACLs enforce.
questions.answer: Your isolated network: CIDR, subnets, route tables, gateways. Public subnets have a route to an IGW; private do not. Security groups and NACLs enforce.

questions.rubric: SG: stateful, ENI-level, allow-only. NACL: stateless, subnet-level, allow/deny. You almost always live on SGs; NACLs for extra subnet deny.
questions.answer: SG: stateful, ENI-level, allow-only. NACL: stateless, subnet-level, allow/deny. You almost always live on SGs; NACLs for extra subnet deny.

questions.text: Why do private subnets need a NAT gateway?
questions.rubric: To reach the internet for patches/APIs without being reachable inbound. NAT lives in public subnets. Cost and AZ pinning: one NAT per AZ for HA.
questions.answer: To reach the internet for patches/APIs without being reachable inbound. NAT lives in public subnets. Cost and AZ pinning: one NAT per AZ for HA.

questions.rubric: The VPC's door to the public internet. Attach it and give public subnets a default route to it. IPv6 uses an Egress-Only IGW for outbound-only.
questions.answer: The VPC's door to the public internet. Attach it and give public subnets a default route to it. IPv6 uses an Egress-Only IGW for outbound-only.

questions.rubric: Peering is 1:1, non-transitive. TGW is a hub that routes many VPCs and on-prem. At 3+ VPCs, TGW beats a mesh of peerings.
questions.answer: Peering is 1:1, non-transitive. TGW is a hub that routes many VPCs and on-prem. At 3+ VPCs, TGW beats a mesh of peerings.

questions.rubric: Expose a service via NLB + VPC endpoint so clients reach it privately without peering or public IPs. Good for SaaS in your VPC. Endpoints have a cost.
questions.answer: Expose a service via NLB + VPC endpoint so clients reach it privately without peering or public IPs. Good for SaaS in your VPC. Endpoints have a cost.

questions.rubric: Gateway: S3 and DynamoDB, route-table based, free-ish. Interface: ENI + PrivateLink, most AWS APIs, you pay hourly and GB. Use them to keep traffic off the NAT/internet.
questions.answer: Gateway: S3 and DynamoDB, route-table based, free-ish. Interface: ENI + PrivateLink, most AWS APIs, you pay hourly and GB. Use them to keep traffic off the NAT/internet.

questions.rubric: RDS is managed MySQL/Postgres/etc. Aurora is AWS's engine: faster failover, storage-auto-grow, more readers. Aurora Serverless v2 for spiky. Cost model differs — measure.
questions.answer: RDS is managed MySQL/Postgres/etc. Aurora is AWS's engine: faster failover, storage-auto-grow, more readers. Aurora Serverless v2 for spiky. Cost model differs — measure.

questions.text: What does RDS Multi-AZ actually give you?
questions.rubric: Synchronous standby in another AZ, automatic failover. Not a read replica (that's async, for reads/DR). You still need backups and a failover runbook.
questions.answer: Synchronous standby in another AZ, automatic failover. Not a read replica (that's async, for reads/DR). You still need backups and a failover runbook.

questions.text: What is a read replica for?
questions.rubric: Async extra reads and cross-region DR. Replication lag is real — do not send read-your-write to a replica without checking lag. Promotion is a DR step.
questions.answer: Async extra reads and cross-region DR. Replication lag is real — do not send read-your-write to a replica without checking lag. Promotion is a DR step.

questions.text: How do you model DynamoDB keys?
questions.rubric: One table, partition key + optional sort key, access patterns first. GSIs for alternate queries. Do not treat it like RDS. Hot partitions kill you — high cardinality PKs.
questions.answer: One table, partition key + optional sort key, access patterns first. GSIs for alternate queries. Do not treat it like RDS. Hot partitions kill you — high cardinality PKs.

questions.text: What is DynamoDB eventual versus strong consistency?
questions.rubric: Default reads can be stale by milliseconds. Strong consistent reads (same region, extra cost/latency) on the main table, not on GSI. Fine for caches; money/ledger may want strong or transactions.
questions.answer: Default reads can be stale by milliseconds. Strong consistent reads (same region, extra cost/latency) on the main table, not on GSI. Fine for caches; money/ledger may want strong or transactions.

questions.rubric: LSI: same partition key, different sort, must be created with the table, strong consistency possible. GSI: new PK, eventual, add later, you pay for projected attrs. GSI is the usual tool.
questions.answer: LSI: same partition key, different sort, must be created with the table, strong consistency possible. GSI: new PK, eventual, add later, you pay for projected attrs. GSI is the usual tool.

questions.rubric: Expiry timestamp; items disappear later, not instantly. Not a legal-hold delete. Use it for sessions and caches. Deleted items can stream.
questions.answer: Expiry timestamp; items disappear later, not instantly. Not a legal-hold delete. Use it for sessions and caches. Deleted items can stream.

questions.rubric: Redis: data structures, persistence, failover, pub/sub. Memcached: simple cache, multithreaded. Almost always Redis unless you have a Memcached-shaped client already.
questions.answer: Redis: data structures, persistence, failover, pub/sub. Memcached: simple cache, multithreaded. Almost always Redis unless you have a Memcached-shaped client already.

questions.rubric: CDN: cache at edges, TLS, WAF, origin shield. OAC to S3 so the bucket stays private. Cache keys and TTLs are the design. Not a substitute for app-level auth.
questions.answer: CDN: cache at edges, TLS, WAF, origin shield. OAC to S3 so the bucket stays private. Cache keys and TTLs are the design. Not a substitute for app-level auth.

questions.text: Which two Route 53 routing policies do you actually use?
questions.rubric: Failover (health-checked primary/secondary), latency, weighted (canaries), geolocation. Alias to ALB/CloudFront. Health checks plus TTL are the gotcha.
questions.answer: Failover (health-checked primary/secondary), latency, weighted (canaries), geolocation. Alias to ALB/CloudFront. Health checks plus TTL are the gotcha.

questions.text: What is a KMS CMK versus an AWS-owned key?
questions.rubric: CMK: you own policy, rotation, CloudTrail decrypt events. AWS-owned: no insight. SSE-KMS on S3/EBS uses a CMK. Grants and key policies plus IAM must both allow.
questions.answer: CMK: you own policy, rotation, CloudTrail decrypt events. AWS-owned: no insight. SSE-KMS on S3/EBS uses a CMK. Grants and key policies plus IAM must both allow.

questions.text: Secrets Manager versus SSM Parameter Store?
questions.rubric: Secrets Manager: rotation for RDS/etc, higher price. SSM SecureString: cheaper params, KMS encrypted. Don't put secrets in Lambda env or AMI.
questions.answer: Secrets Manager: rotation for RDS/etc, higher price. SSM SecureString: cheaper params, KMS encrypted. Don't put secrets in Lambda env or AMI.

questions.rubric: Audit API calls. Org trail to a locked S3 bucket. Without it you cannot investigate. It is not application logs — that's CloudWatch Logs.
questions.answer: Audit API calls. Org trail to a locked S3 bucket. Without it you cannot investigate. It is not application logs — that's CloudWatch Logs.

questions.text: What do you put in CloudWatch versus X-Ray versus logs?
questions.rubric: Metrics/alarms in CloudWatch, traces in X-Ray/OTLP, logs in Log Groups (or OpenSearch). Alarms on SLIs, not on every debug line. Retention and ingestion cost.
questions.answer: Metrics/alarms in CloudWatch, traces in X-Ray/OTLP, logs in Log Groups (or OpenSearch). Alarms on SLIs, not on every debug line. Retention and ingestion cost.

questions.rubric: Records resource configuration and checks rules (encrypted volumes, public buckets). Not a SIEM. Good for compliance drift.
questions.answer: Records resource configuration and checks rules (encrypted volumes, public buckets). Not a SIEM. Good for compliance drift.

questions.rubric: Managed threat detection on CloudTrail, VPC flow, DNS. Findings, not prevention. Pair with Security Hub and response playbooks.
questions.answer: Managed threat detection on CloudTrail, VPC flow, DNS. Findings, not prevention. Pair with Security Hub and response playbooks.

questions.rubric: ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway. Managed rule groups plus your rate limits. WAF is not auth. Put it at the edge you actually expose.
questions.answer: ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway. Managed rule groups plus your rate limits. WAF is not auth. Put it at the edge you actually expose.

questions.text: When is Cognito the right auth?
questions.rubric: Managed user pools / IdP for app users. Not a replacement for IAM on AWS APIs. JWT to your API, IAM roles for AWS resources via identity pools when needed.
questions.answer: Managed user pools / IdP for app users. Not a replacement for IAM on AWS APIs. JWT to your API, IAM roles for AWS resources via identity pools when needed.

questions.rubric: ECS: less Kubernetes, AWS-native, Fargate easy. EKS: Kubernetes portability and ecosystem, more ops. If you don't need k8s APIs, ECS is less load.
questions.answer: ECS: less Kubernetes, AWS-native, Fargate easy. EKS: Kubernetes portability and ecosystem, more ops. If you don't need k8s APIs, ECS is less load.

questions.rubric: No patching AMIs, scale to zero-ish, pay for vCPU/RAM. Limits on privileged/daemon patterns. EC2 launch type when you need GPUs, bursting, or daemons.
questions.answer: No patching AMIs, scale to zero-ish, pay for vCPU/RAM. Limits on privileged/daemon patterns. EC2 launch type when you need GPUs, bursting, or daemons.

questions.rubric: IAM Roles for Service Accounts: a pod assumes a role via OIDC, not a node instance role. Least privilege per service. Pod Identity is the newer sibling.
questions.answer: IAM Roles for Service Accounts: a pod assumes a role via OIDC, not a node instance role. Least privilege per service. Pod Identity is the newer sibling.

questions.rubric: CFN is native. CDK generates CFN in real languages. Terraform is multi-cloud, its own state. Don't mix three without a reason. State and blast radius are the interview.
questions.answer: CFN is native. CDK generates CFN in real languages. Terraform is multi-cloud, its own state. Don't mix three without a reason. State and blast radius are the interview.

questions.rubric: It can contain secrets and is the mapping to real resources. Remote state with lock (S3+Dynamo or Terraform Cloud). Never commit it. Drift vs apply carefully.
questions.answer: It can contain secrets and is the mapping to real resources. Remote state with lock (S3+Dynamo or Terraform Cloud). Never commit it. Drift vs apply carefully.

questions.text: How do you do blue/green on AWS?
questions.rubric: Two fleets (ECS/ASG/Lambda aliases/RDS swap). Shift traffic via weighted Route 53, ALB, or CodeDeploy. Keep a rollback. Databases need expand/contract, not just a DNS flip.
questions.answer: Two fleets (ECS/ASG/Lambda aliases/RDS swap). Shift traffic via weighted Route 53, ALB, or CodeDeploy. Keep a rollback. Databases need expand/contract, not just a DNS flip.

questions.text: How is a canary deploy different from blue/green?
questions.rubric: A small % of traffic (Lambda alias, CodeDeploy, weighted target) then ramp. Faster blast-radius limit. Need metrics to abort. Blue/green is 0/100 cutover.
questions.answer: A small % of traffic (Lambda alias, CodeDeploy, weighted target) then ramp. Faster blast-radius limit. Need metrics to abort. Blue/green is 0/100 cutover.

questions.rubric: Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability. Use them as a review checklist, not a slogan.
questions.answer: Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability. Use them as a review checklist, not a slogan.

questions.rubric: RPO: how much data you can lose (backup frequency). RTO: how long you can be down. Multi-AZ RDS improves RTO; backups set RPO. Cross-region is a different pair of numbers.
questions.answer: RPO: how much data you can lose (backup frequency). RTO: how long you can be down. Multi-AZ RDS improves RTO; backups set RPO. Cross-region is a different pair of numbers.

questions.text: How do you back up a production AWS app?
questions.rubric: RDS snapshots + PITR, Dynamo on-demand/PITR, EBS snapshots, S3 versioning+replication. Test restores. Backup = encrypted, another account/region for ransomware.
questions.answer: RDS snapshots + PITR, Dynamo on-demand/PITR, EBS snapshots, S3 versioning+replication. Test restores. Backup = encrypted, another account/region for ransomware.

questions.text: What three AWS cost controls do you actually use?
questions.rubric: Tags + Cost Explorer/CUR, budgets/anomalies, rightsizing, GP3 vs io2, S3 lifecycle, Graviton, Savings Plans/RIs, turn off idle. Cost is an architecture requirement.
questions.answer: Tags + Cost Explorer/CUR, budgets/anomalies, rightsizing, GP3 vs io2, S3 lifecycle, Graviton, Savings Plans/RIs, turn off idle. Cost is an architecture requirement.

questions.rubric: ARM instances, better price/perf for many Linux workloads. Need multi-arch containers. Easy win if your stack is not x86-only binaries.
questions.answer: ARM instances, better price/perf for many Linux workloads. Need multi-arch containers. Easy win if your stack is not x86-only binaries.

questions.rubric: Fault-tolerant, interruptible workers (batch, CI, stateless ASG with mixed policy). Not for a single-node database. Handle 2-minute interruption notices.
questions.answer: Fault-tolerant, interruptible workers (batch, CI, stateless ASG with mixed policy). Not for a single-node database. Handle 2-minute interruption notices.

questions.rubric: EBS: block, one AZ, one instance (mostly). EFS: NFS, multi-AZ, concurrent. S3: object, infinite, HTTP. Don't put shared web assets on EBS.
questions.answer: EBS: block, one AZ, one instance (mostly). EFS: NFS, multi-AZ, concurrent. S3: object, infinite, HTTP. Don't put shared web assets on EBS.

questions.text: What is an AMI in a pipeline?
questions.rubric: A versioned machine image. Bake with Packer/Image Builder, no snowflakes. Launch templates point at the AMI. Patch by baking a new one, not SSH.
questions.answer: A versioned machine image. Bake with Packer/Image Builder, no snowflakes. Launch templates point at the AMI. Patch by baking a new one, not SSH.

questions.rubric: Session-token instance metadata so SSRF cannot steal the role as easily. Hop limit 1. Require IMDSv2 on launch templates.
questions.answer: Session-token instance metadata so SSRF cannot steal the role as easily. Hop limit 1. Require IMDSv2 on launch templates.

questions.rubric: A route to an IGW, not the name. Instances also need a public IP. Private subnets use NAT. Naming "public" without the route is a lie.
questions.answer: A route to an IGW, not the name. Instances also need a public IP. Private subnets use NAT. Naming "public" without the route is a lie.

questions.text: Why do NACL denies break TCP return traffic?
questions.rubric: NACLs are stateless: you must allow ephemeral return ports inbound. SGs remember the connection. This is why people avoid NACLs for allow-lists.
questions.answer: NACLs are stateless: you must allow ephemeral return ports inbound. SGs remember the connection. This is why people avoid NACLs for allow-lists.

questions.rubric: Accept/reject metadata for ENI traffic, not payloads. Send to S3/CloudWatch. Forensics and "is the NACL dropping me." Cost at high PPS.
questions.answer: Accept/reject metadata for ENI traffic, not payloads. Send to S3/CloudWatch. Forensics and "is the NACL dropping me." Cost at high PPS.

questions.rubric: Blast radius, billing, SCPs, separate prod/nonprod. One account is a single IAM/compromise domain. Log archive and security tooling accounts are the usual skeleton.
questions.answer: Blast radius, billing, SCPs, separate prod/nonprod. One account is a single IAM/compromise domain. Log archive and security tooling accounts are the usual skeleton.

questions.rubric: Opinionated multi-account landing zone: SSO, logging, baseline. Start there instead of hand-rolling Organizations if you are new to multi-account.
questions.answer: Opinionated multi-account landing zone: SSO, logging, baseline. Start there instead of hand-rolling Organizations if you are new to multi-account.

questions.text: IAM Identity Center versus IAM users?
questions.rubric: SSO/Identity Center for humans (workforce IdP). IAM users for a few break-glass. Apps use roles. Long-lived IAM user keys for people are a smell.
questions.answer: SSO/Identity Center for humans (workforce IdP). IAM users for a few break-glass. Apps use roles. Long-lived IAM user keys for people are a smell.

questions.rubric: A max-permissions policy on a principal so they cannot escalate beyond it, even if they can create policies. Used when you let a team mint roles.
questions.answer: A max-permissions policy on a principal so they cannot escalate beyond it, even if they can create policies. Used when you let a team mint roles.

questions.text: How do you know what is in a huge bucket?
questions.rubric: S3 Inventory reports, CloudTrail data events, Access Analyzer. Listing 10B keys with ListObjects is the wrong tool.
questions.answer: S3 Inventory reports, CloudTrail data events, Access Analyzer. Listing 10B keys with ListObjects is the wrong tool.

questions.text: What is S3 Object Lock / WORM?
questions.rubric: Compliance retention: objects cannot be deleted until the period ends. Ransomware and regulated data. Needs versioning. Different from ordinary versioning.
questions.answer: Compliance retention: objects cannot be deleted until the period ends. Ransomware and regulated data. Needs versioning. Different from ordinary versioning.

questions.rubric: Kinesis: ordered streams, multiple consumers, replay, shards. SQS: competing consumers, simpler, no replay after delete. Clickstream → Kinesis; work queue → SQS.
questions.answer: Kinesis: ordered streams, multiple consumers, replay, shards. SQS: competing consumers, simpler, no replay after delete. Clickstream → Kinesis; work queue → SQS.

questions.text: When are Step Functions better than a homegrown worker?
questions.rubric: Visual orchestrations, retries, catch, audit, long-running (Standard) vs high-rate (Express). Don't put business SQL in ASL. Callbacks for humans.
questions.answer: Visual orchestrations, retries, catch, audit, long-running (Standard) vs high-rate (Express). Don't put business SQL in ASL. Callbacks for humans.

questions.text: What is an event-driven AWS shape?
questions.rubric: S3/EventBridge/SQS/Lambda loosely coupled. Failure isolation, but harder tracing. You need correlation ids and idempotency. Not always simpler than a service.
questions.answer: S3/EventBridge/SQS/Lambda loosely coupled. Failure isolation, but harder tracing. You need correlation ids and idempotency. Not always simpler than a service.

questions.text: How do you make Lambda consumers idempotent?
questions.rubric: Dedup key in Dynamo with TTL, or SQS FIFO group, or S3 object key as id. At-least-once is the default. Exactly-once is an application property.
questions.answer: Dedup key in Dynamo with TTL, or SQS FIFO group, or S3 object key as id. At-least-once is the default. Exactly-once is an application property.

questions.text: When should Lambda be in a VPC?
questions.rubric: When it must reach RDS/ElastiCache privately. Otherwise skip VPC to avoid ENI cold starts (better than it was, still a reason). Use RDS Proxy for connection storms.
questions.answer: When it must reach RDS/ElastiCache privately. Otherwise skip VPC to avoid ENI cold starts (better than it was, still a reason). Use RDS Proxy for connection storms.

questions.rubric: Connection pooling in front of RDS so Lambda/microservices don't exhaust max_connections. Failover-aware. Extra hop and cost — use when conn count is the problem.
questions.answer: Connection pooling in front of RDS so Lambda/microservices don't exhaust max_connections. Failover-aware. Extra hop and cost — use when conn count is the problem.

hints: Steady load may be cheaper provisioned.
questions.rubric: v2 scales ACU with load, good for spiky/dev. Provisioned is predictable and often cheaper at steady high load. Cold-ish scale-up still exists — measure.
questions.answer: v2 scales ACU with load, good for spiky/dev. Provisioned is predictable and often cheaper at steady high load. Cold-ish scale-up still exists — measure.

questions.rubric: Serverless SQL over S3 (Iceberg/Parquet). Pay per TB scanned. Partition and columnar files or you burn money. Not for millisecond OLTP.
questions.answer: Serverless SQL over S3 (Iceberg/Parquet). Pay per TB scanned. Partition and columnar files or you burn money. Not for millisecond OLTP.

questions.rubric: ETL (Spark), Data Catalog, crawlers. Heavy. For small jobs, Lambda or Athena CTAS may be enough. Catalog is the useful bit for Athena.
questions.answer: ETL (Spark), Data Catalog, crawlers. Heavy. For small jobs, Lambda or Athena CTAS may be enough. Catalog is the useful bit for Athena.

questions.text: When is Redshift the right warehouse?
questions.rubric: Columnar, large analytic joins, BI. Not a replacement for RDS OLTP or for S3+Athena ad hoc if the team is small. RA3 separates storage/compute.
questions.answer: Columnar, large analytic joins, BI. Not a replacement for RDS OLTP or for S3+Athena ad hoc if the team is small. RA3 separates storage/compute.

questions.text: OpenSearch on AWS is for what?
questions.rubric: Full-text, logs, kNN. Ops-heavy (or serverless). Don't make it your primary system of record. Index mapping is the design.
questions.answer: Full-text, logs, kNN. Ops-heavy (or serverless). Don't make it your primary system of record. Index mapping is the design.

questions.rubric: SageMaker: training, endpoints, pipelines, ground truth — more AWS glue. ECS/EKS: custom serving (vLLM). Pick based on team skill and GPU packing, not branding.
questions.answer: SageMaker: training, endpoints, pipelines, ground truth — more AWS glue. ECS/EKS: custom serving (vLLM). Pick based on team skill and GPU packing, not branding.

questions.text: What is Bedrock in an architecture?
questions.rubric: Managed FMs via API, IAM, optional Guardrails and Knowledge Bases. No GPU ops. Trade control of the runtime for speed-to-market. Still need your eval and RAG design.
questions.answer: Managed FMs via API, IAM, optional Guardrails and Knowledge Bases. No GPU ops. Trade control of the runtime for speed-to-market. Still need your eval and RAG design.

questions.text: How do you stop a cost surprise?
questions.rubric: Budgets + anomaly detection + service quotas + deny in SCP for expensive unused regions. Tag everything. Lambda/Athena unbounded scans are classic blowups.
questions.answer: Budgets + anomaly detection + service quotas + deny in SCP for expensive unused regions. Tag everything. Lambda/Athena unbounded scans are classic blowups.

questions.text: What is the AWS shared responsibility model?
questions.rubric: AWS secures the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, regions). You secure in the cloud: IAM, data, OS patches on EC2, encryption, network ACLs. SaaS (S3, Lambda) shifts more OS work to AWS; EC2 leaves it with you.
questions.answer: AWS secures the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, regions). You secure in the cloud: IAM, data, OS patches on EC2, encryption, network ACLs. SaaS (S3, Lambda) shifts more OS work to AWS; EC2 leaves it with you.

questions.text: What is an IAM instance profile?
questions.rubric: The wrapper that lets an EC2 instance assume a role via IMDS. Apps on the box call the metadata service and get temporary creds. No long-lived keys on disk.
questions.answer: The wrapper that lets an EC2 instance assume a role via IMDS. Apps on the box call the metadata service and get temporary creds. No long-lived keys on disk.

questions.text: What is an identity-based policy versus a resource-based policy?
hints: On the principal vs on the resource.
questions.rubric: Identity-based attaches to a user/role/group (what the principal may do). Resource-based attaches to the resource (S3 bucket, KMS key, SQS) and says who may call it. Cross-account almost always needs the resource policy.
questions.answer: Identity-based attaches to a user/role/group (what the principal may do). Resource-based attaches to the resource (S3 bucket, KMS key, SQS) and says who may call it. Cross-account almost always needs the resource policy.

questions.text: What is an S3 lifecycle rule for?
questions.rubric: Transition or expire objects by prefix/tag/age: Standard → IA → Glacier → delete. Use it for logs and unknown-access data. Test restores before you Glacier production backups.
questions.answer: Transition or expire objects by prefix/tag/age: Standard → IA → Glacier → delete. Use it for logs and unknown-access data. Test restores before you Glacier production backups.

questions.rubric: Async copy of new objects to another region/bucket. Versioning must be on. It is not a backup by itself (deletes can replicate). Pair with Object Lock if you need immutability.
questions.answer: Async copy of new objects to another region/bucket. Versioning must be on. It is not a backup by itself (deletes can replicate). Pair with Object Lock if you need immutability.

questions.text: When do you use a bucket policy instead of an IAM policy?
questions.rubric: When the control belongs on the bucket: public access, cross-account, or "deny unencrypted puts." IAM says what a role can do; the bucket policy is the resource's last word.
questions.answer: When the control belongs on the bucket: public access, cross-account, or "deny unencrypted puts." IAM says what a role can do; the bucket policy is the resource's last word.

questions.rubric: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers. Too short: double processing. Too long: slow retries on crash. Pair with idempotent handlers and a DLQ.
questions.answer: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers. Too short: double processing. Too long: slow retries on crash. Pair with idempotent handlers and a DLQ.

questions.rubric: One publish, many subscriptions (SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email). Each consumer gets its own retry/DLQ. Use it when several independent systems must see the same event.
questions.answer: One publish, many subscriptions (SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email). Each consumer gets its own retry/DLQ. Use it when several independent systems must see the same event.

questions.text: What is reserved versus provisioned Lambda concurrency?
questions.rubric: Reserved: a cap that also guarantees that pool — protects the account limit from noisy functions. Provisioned: keep warm environments ready (cost) to kill cold starts. Different knobs.
questions.answer: Reserved: a cap that also guarantees that pool — protects the account limit from noisy functions. Provisioned: keep warm environments ready (cost) to kill cold starts. Different knobs.

questions.text: How do you handle failed Lambda async invokes?
questions.rubric: DLQ (SQS/SNS) or Lambda Destinations on failure, plus retries with backoff. On-failure destination gives you the error payload. Do not only look at CloudWatch.
questions.answer: DLQ (SQS/SNS) or Lambda Destinations on failure, plus retries with backoff. On-failure destination gives you the error payload. Do not only look at CloudWatch.

questions.rubric: Incremental, S3-backed point-in-time of a volume. Crash-consistent unless you freeze the filesystem. Copy snapshots across regions for DR. Snapshots are not a running replica.
questions.answer: Incremental, S3-backed point-in-time of a volume. Crash-consistent unless you freeze the filesystem. Copy snapshots across regions for DR. Snapshots are not a running replica.

questions.text: When do you pick Direct Connect over a VPN?
questions.rubric: When you need consistent bandwidth and lower jitter to on-prem, and can wait for a circuit. VPN is faster to stand up and a backup path. Many shops run both.
questions.answer: When you need consistent bandwidth and lower jitter to on-prem, and can wait for a circuit. VPN is faster to stand up and a backup path. Many shops run both.

questions.text: What is a Route 53 alias versus a CNAME?
questions.rubric: Alias is AWS-specific, works at the zone apex, no extra charge to AWS targets (ALB, CloudFront, S3 website). CNAME cannot sit at the apex. Alias is the usual answer for apex → ALB.
questions.answer: Alias is AWS-specific, works at the zone apex, no extra charge to AWS targets (ALB, CloudFront, S3 website). CNAME cannot sit at the apex. Alias is the usual answer for apex → ALB.

questions.text: What is Shield versus WAF versus GuardDuty?
questions.rubric: Shield: DDoS (Standard free, Advanced paid). WAF: Layer-7 rules on ALB/CloudFront/APIGW. GuardDuty: threat findings from CloudTrail/DNS/VPC flow. Complementary, not interchangeable.
questions.answer: Shield: DDoS (Standard free, Advanced paid). WAF: Layer-7 rules on ALB/CloudFront/APIGW. GuardDuty: threat findings from CloudTrail/DNS/VPC flow. Complementary, not interchangeable.

questions.rubric: CVE and network-reachability scanning of EC2, ECR images, and Lambda. It is not a pentest and not GuardDuty. Wire findings into a patch SLA.
questions.answer: CVE and network-reachability scanning of EC2, ECR images, and Lambda. It is not a pentest and not GuardDuty. Wire findings into a patch SLA.

questions.rubric: Discovers sensitive data (PII) in S3 with ML + pattern matching. Use it for unknown buckets, not as the only DLP control. Findings go to Security Hub.
questions.answer: Discovers sensitive data (PII) in S3 with ML + pattern matching. Use it for unknown buckets, not as the only DLP control. Findings go to Security Hub.

questions.rubric: Aggregator and score for GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, partner tools. One place for posture. It does not fix anything — you still need owners and tickets.
questions.answer: Aggregator and score for GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, partner tools. One place for posture. It does not fix anything — you still need owners and tickets.

questions.text: Why Session Manager instead of SSH to EC2?
questions.rubric: No inbound 22, IAM-auth, CloudTrail of sessions, no bastion. Needs SSM agent + instance profile. Bastions still appear when you must SCP files or use older images.
questions.answer: No inbound 22, IAM-auth, CloudTrail of sessions, no bastion. Needs SSM agent + instance profile. Bastions still appear when you must SCP files or use older images.

questions.rubric: Savings Plans discount compute usage (EC2/Fargate/Lambda) with more flexibility on instance family. Classic RIs are more rigid but can still win for a fixed RDS size. Measure before you buy.
questions.answer: Savings Plans discount compute usage (EC2/Fargate/Lambda) with more flexibility on instance family. Classic RIs are more rigid but can still win for a fixed RDS size. Measure before you buy.

questions.text: Why does tagging matter in AWS interviews?
questions.rubric: Cost allocation, blast-radius, and automation (backup, stop-dev). Untagged resources are unowned. Enforce with Config/SCP; do not hope people remember.
questions.answer: Cost allocation, blast-radius, and automation (backup, stop-dev). Untagged resources are unowned. Enforce with Config/SCP; do not hope people remember.

questions.rubric: On-demand: pay per request, handles unknown spikes, higher unit price. Provisioned + autoscaling: cheaper at steady load. Switch when the bill and the traffic shape say so.
questions.answer: On-demand: pay per request, handles unknown spikes, higher unit price. Provisioned + autoscaling: cheaper at steady load. Switch when the bill and the traffic shape say so.

questions.rubric: A write-through cache in front of DynamoDB for microsecond reads. Extra moving part, eventual with your table. Use it when hot keys dominate; not a substitute for a bad key design.
questions.answer: A write-through cache in front of DynamoDB for microsecond reads. Extra moving part, eventual with your table. Use it when hot keys dominate; not a substitute for a bad key design.

questions.rubric: Private container registry: IAM auth, scan-on-push, replication, immutable tags. Deploy by digest. It is not a build system — CodeBuild/GitHub Actions push to it.
questions.answer: Private container registry: IAM auth, scan-on-push, replication, immutable tags. Deploy by digest. It is not a build system — CodeBuild/GitHub Actions push to it.

questions.text: When is CodePipeline the right CI versus GitHub Actions?
questions.rubric: When you want AWS-native deploy to CodeDeploy/ECS/CFN with IAM in-account. GitHub Actions is usually nicer for build UX; still assume a role with OIDC to deploy. Many teams mix both.
questions.answer: When you want AWS-native deploy to CodeDeploy/ECS/CFN with IAM in-account. GitHub Actions is usually nicer for build UX; still assume a role with OIDC to deploy. Many teams mix both.

questions.rubric: Functions: tiny, <1ms, viewer-request/response, no network. Lambda@Edge: heavier, origin events too, more latency. Default to Functions for header rewrites.
questions.answer: Functions: tiny, <1ms, viewer-request/response, no network. Lambda@Edge: heavier, origin events too, more latency. Default to Functions for header rewrites.

questions.rubric: Anycast IPs that enter AWS's network close to the user, then to regional ALBs. Not a CDN (no cache). Use for TCP/UDP apps that need static IPs and fast failover.
questions.answer: Anycast IPs that enter AWS's network close to the user, then to regional ALBs. Not a CDN (no cache). Use for TCP/UDP apps that need static IPs and fast failover.

questions.rubric: Standard: long-running, exactly-once, one year, visual history. Express: high-rate, at-least-once, cheap, short. Async business workflows → Standard; IoT/clickstream → Express.
questions.answer: Standard: long-running, exactly-once, one year, visual history. Express: high-rate, at-least-once, cheap, short. Async business workflows → Standard; IoT/clickstream → Express.

questions.rubric: Primary in one region, read replicas in others with ~1s lag, promoted on disaster. Not multi-writer. App must handle read-after-write if it reads a replica region.
questions.answer: Primary in one region, read replicas in others with ~1s lag, promoted on disaster. Not multi-writer. App must handle read-after-write if it reads a replica region.

questions.rubric: Multi-active replication across regions. Last-writer-wins by timestamp. Design for conflict; do not assume a worldwide unique counter without a single writer.
questions.answer: Multi-active replication across regions. Last-writer-wins by timestamp. Design for conflict; do not assume a worldwide unique counter without a single writer.

questions.rubric: Resource Access Manager: share subnets, Transit Gateway, Route 53 resolver rules across accounts without copying. Core to a hub-and-spoke landing zone.
questions.answer: Resource Access Manager: share subnets, Transit Gateway, Route 53 resolver rules across accounts without copying. Core to a hub-and-spoke landing zone.

questions.text: What is IAM Access Analyzer for?
questions.rubric: Finds resource policies that grant external access (S3, KMS, IAM roles). Use it in CI on policy diffs. It does not prove least privilege internally.
questions.answer: Finds resource policies that grant external access (S3, KMS, IAM roles). Use it in CI on policy diffs. It does not prove least privilege internally.

questions.rubric: The same stack rolled to many accounts/regions from the org. How Control Tower and platform teams push baseline IAM, logging, and guardrails. Failures are per-target.
questions.answer: The same stack rolled to many accounts/regions from the org. How Control Tower and platform teams push baseline IAM, logging, and guardrails. Failures are per-target.

questions.text: What is Karpenter versus the cluster autoscaler?
questions.rubric: Karpenter provisions right-sized nodes from unschedulable pods, fast, without ASG node groups. Cluster Autoscaler scales existing ASGs. EKS shops often move to Karpenter for bin-packing.
questions.answer: Karpenter provisions right-sized nodes from unschedulable pods, fast, without ASG node groups. Cluster Autoscaler scales existing ASGs. EKS shops often move to Karpenter for bin-packing.
